main_body: Marble column: a grey-white shaft (rows 16-40) between a wide capital (rows 9-15) and a base (rows 41-47)
top_band: Light white band on the capital at rows 10-11, only about 2 rows. It is a flat rectangular strip with no ellipse or surface depth. The shaft has no top surface of its own.
evidence: Reading down the centre column: a dark outline at row 9, then a white band at rows 10-11, then a grey capital face at rows 12-14 with a light line, then a dark underside at row 15, then the shaft from row 16 as a vertical gradient. The cap is a flat rectangular band only 2 rows tall, like the red 'column: flat band cap' in the guide, not the green ellipse cap. No distinct front-edge line or eave shadow reads as a top surface. The base repeats the same thin band at rows 41-42. This is a front elevation with thin rim bands, so it fails.

style.evidence: The shaft is a smooth vertical gradient of about 4 grey steps, with no grain, veining, chips or speckle. The capital and base are flat fills with a single highlight line. The outline is a dark purple-grey lean, which is acceptable, but the piece is much thinner than the stall and well references, which carry many colours and texture per tile. Most tiles hold only 3-5 colours.
